text.p: Barney's Inc said Friday it filed a motion seeking Bankruptcy Court approval to offer a termination fee and expense reimbursement protections to an acceptable investor who submits an approved investment proposal in connection with the recapitalization of the company.

The company said it is prepared to offer up to $1.5 million in "actual, reasonable, fully-documented out-of-pocket expenses" and up to $8.5 million in termination fees to an investor who submits an approved investment proposal that is then terminated as a result of the consummation of an agreement with an alternate acceptable investor that submits a higher and better offer.
The company said that to receive such protection, investor proposals must be submitted by May 8, or 14 days after the Bankruptcy Court approves the motion, which it is scheduled to hear on April 24.
Barney's, which has been in bankruptcy for more than a year, is locked in a dispute with Japanese partner Isetan Co Ltd over various issues, including licensing.
